title: End-Time Visions: The Road to Armageddon?
author: Richard Abanes
summary: An evangelical journalist's survey of failed end-time predictions, from the early church to the 1990s, arguing that date-setting and newspaper exegesis have repeatedly harmed believers.

title: When Time Shall Be No More: Prophecy Belief in Modern American Culture
author: Paul Boyer
summary: A Harvard University Press cultural history of American prophecy belief, especially dispensational readings of the Cold War, Israel, Russia, the Common Market and the Middle East.

title: The Pursuit of the Millennium: Revolutionary Millenarians and Mystical Anarchists of the Middle Ages
author: Norman Cohn
summary: A classic history of medieval and Reformation-era millenarian movements, including the flagellants, the Taborites, Thomas Müntzer and the Anabaptist kingdom of Münster.

title: Visions of the End: Apocalyptic Traditions in the Middle Ages
author: Bernard McGinn
summary: An annotated anthology of medieval apocalyptic texts, from the Tiburtine Sibyl and Adso through Joachim of Fiore, the Spiritual Franciscans and Frederick II, with introductions placing each in context.

title: Armageddon Now! The Premillenarian Response to Russia and Israel Since 1917
author: Dwight Wilson
summary: A study, by a Pentecostal historian, of how premillennial writers repeatedly identified current events involving Russia, Israel and the Middle East as fulfilments, and revised those identifications as events changed.

title: The Day and the Hour: Christianity's Perennial Fascination with Predicting the End of the World
author: Francis X. Gumerlock
summary: A chronicle of some two thousand years of Christian predictions that the end was near, arranged century by century with primary-source quotations.

title: 99 Reasons Why No One Knows When Christ Will Return
author: B. J. Oropeza
summary: A short InterVarsity Press book answering date-setting (written in part as a reply to Whisenant and Camping) from Scripture, history and logic.

title: 88 Reasons Why the Rapture Will Be in 1988
author: Edgar C. Whisenant
summary: A booklet by a former NASA engineer arguing that the rapture would occur at Rosh Hashanah, 11–13 September 1988; distributed in millions of copies.
note: Cited as a primary example of date-setting, not as an endorsed interpretation.

title: The Disappointed: Millerism and Millenarianism in the Nineteenth Century
author: Ronald L. Numbers and Jonathan M. Butler (eds.)
summary: Scholarly essays on William Miller, the Millerite movement, the Great Disappointment of 22 October 1844 and the movements that emerged from it.

title: On the Road to Armageddon: How Evangelicals Became Israel's Best Friend
author: Timothy P. Weber
summary: A historian's account of how dispensational premillennialism moved from watching prophetic events to actively supporting Israel, including the 1967 war, the Temple movement and popular prophecy literature.

title: Heaven on Earth: The Varieties of the Millennial Experience
author: Richard Landes
summary: A comparative study of millennial movements by the leading advocate of the view that apocalyptic expectation around the year 1000 was real and widespread, though under-reported by clerical sources.

title: Commentary on Daniel
author: Hippolytus of Rome
summary: The oldest surviving Christian commentary on a biblical book; in book 4 Hippolytus places the incarnation 5,500 years after creation, putting the end around AD 500, and warns against those who led believers out to meet Christ.

title: Ecclesiastical History of the English People (esp. I.32)
author: Bede
summary: Bede's history preserves Pope Gregory the Great's letter of 601 to King Æthelberht of Kent, which warns that the end of the present world is at hand.

title: The Libro de las profecías of Christopher Columbus
author: Christopher Columbus (ed. and trans. Delno C. West and August Kling)
summary: Columbus's notebook of biblical and patristic prophecies, in which he reckons, following Augustine and Pierre d'Ailly, that about 155 years remained of the world's 7,000 years.

title: A Plaine Discovery of the Whole Revelation of Saint John
author: John Napier
summary: A Scottish Protestant historicist commentary by the later inventor of logarithms, identifying the papacy as Antichrist and calculating the day of judgment to fall between 1688 and 1700.

title: Evidence from Scripture and History of the Second Coming of Christ, About the Year 1843
author: William Miller
summary: Miller's lectures arguing from the 2,300 days of Daniel 8:14, dated from 457 BC, that Christ would return about 1843.

title: Apocalypse Delayed: The Story of Jehovah's Witnesses
author: M. James Penton
summary: A history of the Watch Tower movement by a former Witness historian, tracing its successive expectations for 1874, 1914, 1925 and 1975.

title: 1975 in Prophecy!
author: Herbert W. Armstrong
summary: A Radio Church of God booklet describing coming world catastrophe; its title and the church's preaching led members to expect the end around 1975, though the booklet itself avoids an explicit date for Christ's return.

author: Harold Camping
summary: Family Radio president Harold Camping's book arguing from biblical chronology that the end would very probably come in September 1994; the question mark in the title was his own hedge.

title: Four Blood Moons: Something Is About to Change
author: John Hagee
summary: A best-seller linking the lunar eclipse tetrad of 2014–2015, falling on Passover and Tabernacles, to past turning points in Jewish history and to coming events.

title: Blood Moons: Decoding the Imminent Heavenly Signs
author: Mark Biltz
summary: The fuller statement of the blood-moons thesis by the Washington pastor who first popularised it in 2008, reading Genesis 1:14 and Joel 2:31 alongside the Hebrew festival calendar.

title: Armageddon, Oil and the Middle East Crisis
author: John F. Walvoord (with John E. Walvoord)
summary: A popular dispensational account of how Middle East events fit the prophetic programme; the revised edition sold very widely during the 1990–91 Gulf crisis.

title: Ready to Rebuild: The Imminent Plan to Rebuild the Last Days Temple
author: Thomas Ice and Randall Price
summary: Two dispensational scholars survey the Jewish Temple movements and red-heifer research and argue that they set the stage for a future Temple of Daniel 9:27 and 2 Thessalonians 2:4.

title: The End of Days: Fundamentalism and the Struggle for the Temple Mount
author: Gershom Gorenberg
summary: An Israeli journalist's account of how Jewish, Christian and Muslim end-time hopes converge on the Temple Mount, including the red-heifer projects and evangelical support for Temple activists.

title: When Your Money Fails: The '666 System' Is Here
author: Mary Stewart Relfe
summary: A best-selling early example of reading barcodes, credit cards and electronic funds transfer as the coming mark-of-the-beast system.

title: Future Survival
author: Chuck Smith
summary: A book by the founder of Calvary Chapel in which he wrote that, from his understanding of prophecy, he was convinced the Lord would come for his church before the end of 1981, while allowing that he could be wrong.

title: Millions Now Living Will Never Die
author: J. F. Rutherford
summary: The Watch Tower president's lecture and booklet predicting that 1925 would see the return of the ancient worthies such as Abraham, Isaac and Jacob and the beginning of earthly restoration.

title: Famines
author: Joe Hasell and Max Roser (Our World in Data)
summary: A data overview of famine mortality since the 1860s, showing that famine deaths fell sharply in the late twentieth and early twenty-first centuries relative to earlier decades and to population.

title: Why are we having so many earthquakes? Has naturally occurring earthquake activity been increasing?
author: United States Geological Survey
summary: The USGS explains that the number of large earthquakes has stayed fairly constant over the instrumental record, and that apparent increases reflect many more seismograph stations and faster reporting.
note: The page's substance is long-standing USGS guidance; the exact URL could not be re-checked during research because of a rate limit.
